source: What do you intend to do with everyone in Elsinore? With those who survive the coup?
Restore young Hamlet to his rightful throne, and command him as his ruling lord, of course.
From everything Lady Brit has told me, Hamlet is young, malleable, and mad. He will be accepted as an heir to the throne by the nobility, but easily controlled.
Restore the glory of Denmark's ruling house, of course. Given everything Lady Brit has told me, this work is sorely needed.
And from there, we will forge a lasting peace between our two nations, and consume Sweden into this unity with haste.
I intend to act swiftly to save as many lives as possible. I will eliminate only those who directly threaten me.
You, for example.
No. I won't let you kill her.
You can't. She's not the enemy, my lord. I brought her here. She's... she's...
Please. Isn't there any other way?
B-because if not... you're going to have to fight me, too.
Chivalrous, Lady Brit. But I do not murder women indiscriminately.
Brit. That's enough.
Thank you for defending me. But you don't have to anymore. I know what I need to know.
It's strange, so strange I could laugh. You killed me, once. And here we are now, you defending me.
Of all the worlds we could have ended up in, this is the one I least expected.
What are you saying? Stop talking like that! Are you insane?
My lord, please spare her! She's just a girl like me. We never had a choice in any of this.
A-and-- she's not like me. I might be cruel to her, but... she's a good person!
Goodbye for a moment, Brit.
Eliminated by Fortinbras.

source: White her shroud as the mountain snow...
Gerta's dead.
Not now. Please not now. Whatever it is can wait.
There's nothing I need. You don't seem well, my lord.
I am deeply, deeply unwell.
I did all of this for her. Everything. If my wife is gone—what remains of me?
She came to Elsinore far too young. She was just a frightened child. Even then, I found her so striking.
We... my brother and I, we always knew she was to be Hamlet's bride, when all three of us were older. My father made that much clear.
She was to marry him and bear him children to fill out a scant royal line.
But she-- I-- we loved each other.
The only person who ever deemed me worthy of love.
My brother used to beat me. I'm certain no one knows it.
My father forced us to duel each other as children, to train against one another.
Hamlet won every time. He'd come after me later, drag me to the stables, kick me in the gut and leave me there in a pile of hay stinking of urine.
Gerta... she... found... places to hide from Hamlet. Little nooks and crannies. We'd climb into the knotted hole of a tree and curl up asleep under the stars.
She's the only reason I've survived until now.
She had this infinite capacity to love, and to love him, and me, no matter what we did, or how sad she was to be trapped in a foreign land...
I always wanted to free her, to make her happy, and I never knew how.
They all think my brother was a strong King. And I cannot disagree. He was more than strong. He was a brute.
I tried to be a man worthy of being her husband, in the short time we had together. My life's dream achieved, only to lose her like this.
I'm sorry, my lord. It's clear to me how deeply you loved her.
And for what it's worth, it was plain to me how happy you made her in return.
It is the hope of all that they might find a love like that someday.
I've tried to love other women before, women who weren't her, but I couldn't.
She was all I dreamed about. She was all I knew. No woman could hold a candle to Gerta.
But now, after just three short months, Gerta is dead.
Y-you remind me of her in some ways.
You have her cleverness, her curiosity, and her mercy.
I have a favor to ask. It is terribly imprudent.
What did you have in mind?
I... feel... so tired. As though I could sleep for weeks.
But... she always sat with me when falling asleep at night.
She'd lie next to me, embrace me, and wait until I dozed off before she went back to her own chambers.
I know it is inappropriate to ask, and unbecoming of a man in my position. But...
Would you be willing to sit with me a while?
Sit with Claudius as he falls asleep?

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: Here, my lord. Your chambers.
You are a girl no longer.
I have often thought to myself...
M-maybe there's a world where I could love you.
Not the way I loved her. But different.
Sleep now, Claudius. You're not making any sense.
(He's asleep downstairs, at last.)
(Even though I know what he's capable of—what he's done—I still somehow feel terrible for him.)
(I've seldom been in Claudius's chambers, let alone unattended...)
(Right before I left, he mentioned he would send someone to find me later today. I wonder what for.)
I'm sorry, Claudius, but I can't.
I see. Of course. As I said, it was imprudent of me.
Please pardon me. It's been an incredibly strange day.
I need to be alone now.
My lady, the King requests your presence in his private chambers.
He... er... wishes to see you alone and unchaperoned.
Visit Claudius's chambers alone?

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: Please tell the King I'm not available tonight—or at all.
So. You came.
You beckoned, my lord.
I apologize. I am not good at... this.
I pray you'll spare your laughter at my expense.
What is this about?
Would you do the honors of accompanying me for a goblet of wine?
Accompanying you where?
Here, I mean. Er. Joining. Not... accompanying.
If you insist, my lord.
I insist on nothing. This is merely a request.
Yes, and I accepted. But it's rather cold and dreary in here, isn't it?
Hrm... Yes. It is. Dark, too.
I used to go to Gerta's chambers for evenings like this.
The hearth is quite large in there. As you've no doubt noticed, these chambers have only one furnace, down in my private bedchamber.
Your bedchamber is the same way, is it not?
I've often insisted my maids bring the bed-warmer with hot coals—at least in the wintertime.
So have I!
Drat this old, moldy castle. My father had such a love for it.
But sometimes I find the annoyances pile up over the years.
Come. If you don't find it too macabre, let us drink in there. The fire's far warmer.
Certainly warmer.
I never thought I'd be here.
You've not been in my wife's rooms before?
That's not what I mean.
You must think it strange, an old man like me asking for your company.
Perhaps you find me odious.
It is strange. I'm merely unused to seeing you in this way, I suppose.
It's unlike anything I'd ever imagined, Ophelia.
The burden of all this. I never wanted to be King, you know. I just wanted to beat my brother. Just once.
He was so perfect. He could do no wrong—in Gertrude's eyes, in my nephew Hamlet's. And then there was me, his foolish little shadow.
Well, more the fool am I. I am a terrible King. I would throw all this away if I could.
Why did you invite me here?
Are you certain you want to know?
I think so.
I must confess to having suffered some... impure thoughts lately.
In the last year especially, you have grown lovelier than ever before.
It's hard not to notice. Certainly all of the red-blooded men in Elsinore have.
Of course, in her lifetime, my wife occupied the entirety of my world.
I was always urged to take additional lovers, as all men in my position are.
Even your father insisted upon it once or twice. But I always found the notion at odds with who I am.
I loved Gertrude. And only Gertrude. But now I am forced to contend with the possibility that, in her absence, I am only human.
You were very, very kind to me the other night.
You needed help. You were distraught.
Yes. But there was something more there, wasn't there? I felt it strongly. I think—or I hope—you did, too.
And I propose there is now time to explore those feelings further.
Enter a sexual relationship with Claudius?

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: I agree. And I'd like to come to know you in all senses.
Why don't you show me what a King can do?
Cheeky, cheeky girl.
But I warn you, now that you're mine, you won't be going anywhere soon...
(...He's asleep. For now, at least.)
(I lay with the King. It feels like a dream. But it really happened.)
(I wonder what the others will say if they find out. Likely nothing good.)
You flatter me. But I think this has gone on long enough, my lord.
I've no interest in pursuing anything like that with you.
Ah. I see. How inappropriate of me. Of course you wouldn't be.
I have intruded long enough upon your time and graces. I hope you can forgive my transgression.
I'll leave you in peace, now.
My lady, the King requests your presence.
Continue my romantic liaison with Claudius?

context.type: 资料、界面或未定位对白

source: Please tell the King I'm not available tonight.
You beckoned, my King?
How could I stay away after yesterday evening?
I have begun to look forward to—this. Whatever this is.
And I as well, my lord. But, of course... you could come ask for me yourself.
I'm not ready to face the others. I wanted privacy for myself. And for you.
They would understand, I think. But I don't want to have to explain all this to your father. Not yet, at least.
Now then. I have something for you.
I thought it might please you.
It belonged to my mother. I rediscovered it recently.
It's a very old, fine pendant. The jewel laid within is called 'ruby.'
It's beautiful. Thank you, my lord.
You ought to call me Claudius. I find my own title strange on the tongue these days.
Thank you, Claudius. You know, some women would see a gift like this as a promise.
And if it were?
What would you have to say then?
We've only just begun this, whatever this is.
No one has to know. Not yet. But you'd make a fine queen, you know.
That's not what you said when Hamlet and I were together.
Ah. Yes. Call it a little jealousy, that.
Or some misguided attempt to deny my brat of a nephew anything which might validate his behavior further.
And that aside—I'm the King. I do as I please.
I don't know how I feel about this.
Give it some thought. I've spent the entire day mulling over this.
You needn't wear that pendant. But keep it safe. Some day, you might.
Thank you, my l—Claudius. It's beautiful. Truly.
I imagine it glows all the brighter against bare flesh.
Let's find out, shall we?
Yes. Let's.
I cannot accept this gift.
